tools.name: search
tools.description: Use this to check prior work before changing code, and whenever the user asks about earlier sessions; run long investigations in a subagent that returns only findings with session ids. Find the earlier sessions about a test, file, error, library or value: the first call for "has anyone…", "why does…" and "how did we…" questions and before any change. Put 2 to 4 specific words from your task in query (a test name, file path, identifier, error text or component); every word must appear (English inflections share a stem), so a whole sentence finds nothing while its key words do. Results are message excerpts grouped by session with each session_id; open the best one with get. Filters take one value or a list (any of), all must hold: repo_name is host/org/repo as git names the remote, or org/repo or the bare name when only one repository matches; file_prefix with file_operation selects sessions that touched a file. Example, "why does the payments client retry the way it does?": {"query":"payments retry","filters":{"file_prefix":"src/payments","file_operation":"edit"}}.

query.description: Words to find; every word must appear (English stems match). May be empty when a filter is given

filters.description: Narrow by session or message fields. Each key takes one value or a list (any of); every key given must hold

repo_name.description: Sessions in these repositories: host/org/repo, or org/repo or the bare repository name when only one repository matches

user_email.description: Sessions run by these members (exact email)

ingest_api_key_id.description: Sessions uploaded with these ingest API keys (key id, exact); the Install page uses it to show one machine's sessions

tool_name.description: Messages calling or answering these tools, such as Read or Bash

file_prefix.description: Sessions that touched a file whose path starts with this text, such as src/auth/

file_operation.description: Sessions where a file was read, edited, written or deleted; with file_prefix, the same file must match both

since.description: Messages at or after this UTC time (inclusive)

where.description: Up to 10 extra conditions that must all hold, on a message field (tool_name, tool_use_id, content, role, kind, model, or a JSON path inside tool_input) or a session field (harness, title, repo_name, branch, user_email, status)

op.description: eq: exact, case-sensitive, null matches missing; contains and starts_with: literal, case-insensitive; exists: non-null, takes no value

path.description: JSON keys or array positions inside tool_input; only with field tool_input

value.description: Text for text fields; any JSON primitive for a tool_input path

context.description: Neighbouring non-thinking messages either side of each hit

limit.description: Hit messages per page; at most 3 hits per session

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page; null for the first page

tools.name: get
tools.description: Use this to check prior work before changing code, and whenever the user asks about earlier sessions; run long investigations in a subagent that returns only findings with session ids. Open one session by session_id, usually the best search hit: a header (who ran it, harness, model, repository, branch, start, end, status, message, tool call, token, file, commit and reuse counts, tools_used, root_session_id, parent and child sessions) and its messages in seq order with role, kind, tool_name, tool_use_id and content. Each child ref carries parent_tool_use_id, the tool_use_id of the TOOL_USE message here that spawned it (null when unrecorded), so a subagent run reads in place under its call. Bound a range with from/to; when next is not null, pass it as cursor. Example, the first 40 messages: {"session_id":"01a08fd7-9907-72a3-9135-80162670d93a","from":0,"to":40}.

cursor.description: The next value of a previous page; omit to start at from

offset.description: Byte offset inside that message's content

anyOf.description: Position inside a session's messages for continuing a read

kinds.description: Message kinds to return, in seq order. Left out: META, the harness's housekeeping records (tool listings, skill listings, reminders); list it to read them. Default TEXT, THINKING, TOOL_USE, TOOL_RESULT

session_id.description: Session to read, from a search result or the sessions view

tools.name: sql
tools.description: Use this to check prior work before changing code, and whenever the user asks about earlier sessions; run long investigations in a subagent that returns only findings with session ids. Answer questions search cannot, with one read-only ClickHouse SELECT over api_ro: who worked on a repository, which sessions touched a file, counts over time. Views: sessions (session metadata); messages (normalized messages); session_files (observed files: path, ops); session_observed_commits (commit observations); session_tools (tool counts); users (visible contributors); installations (visible devices); repos (visible repository counts); schema_columns (column descriptions); schema_functions (function descriptions). search_messages(q='words') returns uncapped session_id,seq,rank. Discover columns with SELECT * FROM schema_columns WHERE view_name = 'sessions' and every table function this organization can use with SELECT * FROM schema_functions. Limits: 500 rows, 5 seconds. Example, the newest sessions of one repository: {"sql":"SELECT session_id,title,started_at FROM sessions WHERE repo_name = 'github.com/acme/orders-api' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 20"}.

tools.name: dashboard_list
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to view, build or change dashboards. List the organization's dashboards (id, name, tile count, flags, updated_at, description), which one is the Home default and the starter tile template ids; read a definition with dashboard_get. Two built-ins always exist: Team overview (captured sessions, search adoption and reuse; the default until an admin picks another) and Team activity (sessions, messages, tool calls, repositories and coding tools per person, for managers). The definition JSON Schema travels as structuredContent.definition_schema.

tools.name: dashboard_get
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to view, build or change dashboards. Read one dashboard by id with its full definition: variables, tiles, SQL, layout and chart options.

tools.name: dashboard_render
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to view, build or change dashboards. Run the queries of a dashboard (by id or an inline definition) with variable values such as {"time_range":"7d","repo":["github.com/org/repo"]} and return each tile's rows. Pass tiles to render a subset. Saved dashboards are served from a cache that a newly published session invalidates; the result says when it was rendered and whether it came from the cache, and refresh: true re-runs the tiles.

items.description: Variable {name, label?, type, default?}: type time_range (default preset 24h|7d|14d|30d|90d|this_week|last_week|this_month|all) exposes {name}_from and {name}_to as DateTime; repo, harness and user expose {name} as Array(String) where empty means all; text exposes {name} as String.

Tile {id, title, description?, layout {x 0-11, y, w 1-12, h 1-40}} plus per type: stat {sql, value?, compare?, unit?}; chart {sql, series_by?, unit?, chart}; table {sql, columns?}; text {markdown}; control {variable}. sql: one ClickHouse SELECT over api_ro, declared variables as {name:Type}. unit: count|ratio|seconds|milliseconds|tokens|usd. chart: allowlisted ECharts option with series (1-20; type line|bar|pie|scatter|gauge|heatmap; encode {x?, y?, value?, itemName?, tooltip?} binds result columns; name?, stack?, smooth?, step?, showSymbol?, symbol?, symbolSize?, connectNulls?, areaStyle?, lineStyle?, itemStyle?, label?, labelLine?, emphasis?, barWidth?, barMaxWidth?, barGap?, radius?, center?, roseType?, xAxisIndex?, yAxisIndex?, min?, max?, progress?, detail?, axisLine?, pointer?, splitLine?, axisLabel?, axisTick?, title?) and xAxis?, yAxis?, legend?, tooltip?, grid?, color?, dataZoom?, visualMap?, polar?, radiusAxis?, angleAxis?. Style blocks: plain JSON, at most three levels, scalar or scalar-array leaves. Unknown keys are rejected.

definition.description: Dashboard definition. dashboard_list names the starter templates and carries the complete JSON Schema as structuredContent.definition_schema; dashboard_get on a built-in shows a complete working definition; dashboard_render validates an inline definition and names the failing path.

variables.description: Values by variable name: a preset (24h|7d|14d|30d|90d|this_week|last_week|this_month|all) or {from, to} in UTC for time_range; a list of strings for repo, harness and user; text for text.

tools.name: dashboard_save
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to view, build or change dashboards. Create or update a dashboard everyone in the organization can see. Start from dashboard_list templates, validate with dashboard_render on an inline definition, then save. Updates need id and revision; only the creator or an organization admin can change a saved dashboard.
